name: Game of Thrones universe
intro: Watch Game of Thrones first — it's the spine of the franchise. House of the Dragon is a prequel set ~200 years earlier; you can start there, but the original series pays off more if you've seen the main saga.

name: Breaking Bad universe
intro: Breaking Bad first, then Better Call Saul — Saul is a prequel but written to reward viewers who already know where everyone ends up. El Camino (the movie) goes last.

entries.note: Prequel — watch after BB for maximum payoff

name: The Walking Dead universe
intro: The flagship series first, then the spin-offs in release order — each assumes you know the world rules even when the timeline jumps.

name: Yellowstone & Taylor Sheridan universe
intro: Yellowstone is the anchor. The prequels 1883 and 1923 fill in the Dutton origin story — watch Yellowstone through at least Season 1 before the prequels for context.

name: Star Trek (modern era)
intro: No single "correct" order across 60 years of Trek — this is the modern streaming-era path: Discovery as a soft entry, then Strange New Worlds and the rest in release order.

name: Marvel Netflix / street-level MCU
intro: The Defenders saga in release order — Daredevil is the crown jewel, but Jessica Jones and Luke Cage interleave cleanly if you watch as they originally dropped.

name: Marvel Disney+ phase
intro: Phase 4 TV in release order — WandaVision kicks off the multiverse thread; Loki and What If? branch from there. No strict episode-level interleaving required.

name: Star Wars live-action TV
intro: The Mandalorian first — it defined the tone. Book of Boba Fett and Ahsoka extend the same era; Andor is a standalone prequel you can slot in anytime after Mando S1.

entries.note: Rebels sequel — more rewarding if you know Clone Wars

name: Doctor Who (2005 revival)
intro: Start with Series 1 (2005) — the Russell T Davies era. New Who is designed for newcomers; you don't need Classic Who first, though it rewards deep cuts.

name: Arrowverse (CW DC)
intro: Arrow first, then the spin-offs in release order. The big crossovers (Crisis on Infinite Earths) land harder if you've followed the main shows through their early seasons.

name: The Office (US) & mockumentary cousins
intro: The US Office stands alone — watch straight through. Parks and Rec shares DNA but no plot dependency; slot it in whenever you finish Scranton.

entries.note: Same mockumentary DNA — no plot tie-in

name: Middle-earth on screen
intro: Peter Jackson's films first if you haven't seen them — Rings of Power is a prequel set in the Second Age and assumes you know what a Ring is.

name: Star Trek (original era)
intro: The pre-2017 saga in broadcast order: Kirk's original five-year mission, then Picard's Next Generation and its two concurrent spin-offs, capped by the Enterprise prequel. The Animated Series is an optional canon coda.

entries.note: Runs concurrent with TNG and Voyager

name: Stargate
intro: Start with the decade-long flagship SG-1, pick up Atlantis as it spins off from SG-1's eighth season, then finish with the darker, serialized Universe.

name: Buffy & the Buffyverse
intro: Watch Buffy straight through and interleave Angel alongside it from Buffy's fourth season — the spin-off runs in parallel and the two trade crossovers.

name: The X-Files universe
intro: The conspiracy saga plus Chris Carter's two sibling series set in the same world — the apocalyptic Millennium and the short-lived spin-off The Lone Gunmen.

name: Avatar: The Last Airbender & Korra
intro: The animated saga in order — Aang's complete journey, then the next Avatar a generation later in The Legend of Korra.

name: Battlestar Galactica (reimagined)
intro: The 2003 miniseries opens the reimagined saga; watch the series through, then the prequel Caprica for how the Cylons began. (The 1978 original is a separate classic.)

name: The Vampire Diaries universe
intro: Start in Mystic Falls with The Vampire Diaries, then follow the Mikaelsons to New Orleans in The Originals, which spins off from the parent show's third season. (Legacies continues the story afterward.)

name: One Chicago (Dick Wolf)
intro: Dick Wolf's interlocking Chicago shows in launch order — Fire first, then the P.D. and Med spin-offs it seeded, all sharing frequent crossovers.

name: Law & Order
intro: The mothership and its New York siblings in launch order — the original ripped-from-the-headlines procedural, the long-running SVU, and Criminal Intent, with regular crossovers.

name: NCIS
intro: The NCIS franchise in launch order — the flagship (itself a JAG spin-off), then its coastal offshoots, each backdoor-piloted from the show before it.

name: CSI: Crime Scene Investigation
intro: The forensic franchise in order — the Las Vegas original, then the Miami and New York spin-offs, and the short-lived Cyber.
